questions.question: Which is the best first step when investigating why a plant is wilting?
options: Observe the plant and gather information
questions.explanation: Careful observation helps frame a testable question.

questions.question: A student tests whether sunlight affects seedling growth. Which factor should be changed deliberately?
options: Type of seed in each pot
Amount of water for each pot
questions.explanation: Change one variable while keeping other conditions the same.

questions.question: Which tool is most suitable for measuring the length of a pencil?
questions.explanation: A ruler measures length.

questions.question: Which unit is appropriate for the length of a classroom?
questions.explanation: Room length is conveniently measured in metres.

questions.question: Why should a measurement be repeated?
options: To check reliability and reduce accidental error
questions.explanation: Repeated measurements help identify unusual readings and improve confidence.

questions.question: Which statement is an observation rather than an explanation?
questions.explanation: An observation records what can be seen directly.

questions.question: A fair test compares two groups of plants. What should be kept the same?
options: Every condition including the tested one
All conditions except the one being tested
questions.explanation: A fair test changes one factor and controls the others.

questions.question: Which is a testable question?
options: Does the amount of water affect bean plant growth?
questions.explanation: A testable question can be investigated through observations or experiments.

questions.question: A beaker contains 35 mL of water. Which tool measures this volume most accurately?
questions.explanation: A graduated cylinder is designed to measure liquid volume.

questions.question: Why should results be recorded in a table?
options: To organise and compare observations clearly
questions.explanation: Tables make patterns and comparisons easier to identify.

questions.question: Which plant part usually absorbs water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil.

questions.question: Which gas do green plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide and water to make food using light energy.

questions.question: What is the main role of leaves in most green plants?
questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll and are the main site of photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which part usually develops into a fruit after fertilisation?
questions.explanation: The flower's ovary develops into the fruit.

questions.question: What is the function of a flower's petals in many plants?
questions.explanation: Bright petals can attract insects and other pollinators.

questions.question: A plant kept in darkness for a long time may become pale because it cannot make enough
questions.explanation: Light is needed for normal chlorophyll formation and photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which of these is most likely dispersed by wind?
options: A heavy coconut with no air space
A seed inside a juicy fruit eaten by birds
questions.explanation: Light seeds with hairs or wings can be carried by air.

questions.question: Which structure carries water from roots towards leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem transports water and minerals through the plant.

questions.question: What is pollination?
options: Growth of a root towards water
Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
Release of water vapour from leaves
questions.explanation: Pollination transfers pollen to the stigma of a flower.

questions.question: Which condition is essential for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires light, water and carbon dioxide; chlorophyll captures light energy.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through blood vessels.

questions.question: Which body system helps us breathe?
questions.explanation: The respiratory system includes airways and lungs.

questions.question: Which part of the skeleton protects the brain?
questions.explanation: The skull surrounds and protects the brain.

questions.question: Which animal is a herbivore?
questions.explanation: Herbivores feed mainly on plants; deer eat leaves and grasses.

questions.question: Which adaptation helps a fish breathe underwater?
questions.explanation: Gills extract dissolved oxygen from water.

questions.question: Which is an example of a vertebrate?
questions.explanation: Vertebrates have a backbone; frogs are amphibian vertebrates.

questions.question: What is the main function of the small intestine?
questions.explanation: Most nutrient absorption occurs in the small intestine.

questions.question: Which joint allows the arm to move in many directions at the shoulder?
questions.explanation: The shoulder's ball-and-socket joint allows movement in several directions.

questions.question: Which relationship is correctly matched?
options: Tick and dog — neither is affected
Bee and flowering plant — mutual benefit
Cactus and desert — both are animals
questions.explanation: Bees gain nectar or pollen while helping pollinate flowers.

questions.question: Why do mammals feed milk to their young?
questions.explanation: Mammalian mothers produce milk to nourish their young.

questions.question: Which nutrient is the body's main immediate source of energy?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are an important energy source.

questions.question: Which food is a good source of protein?
questions.explanation: Pulses such as lentils provide plant protein.

questions.question: Which vitamin is made in the skin with help from sunlight?
questions.explanation: Sunlight helps the skin synthesise vitamin D.

questions.question: Which nutrient helps build and repair body tissues?
questions.explanation: Proteins supply building materials for growth and tissue repair.

questions.question: Why is dietary fibre useful?
options: It supplies more energy than fat
It stops the need for water
It helps food move through the digestive tract
questions.explanation: Fibre supports healthy bowel movement.

questions.question: Which is the best example of a balanced meal?
questions.explanation: A varied meal provides different nutrients.

questions.question: Which practice helps prevent food contamination?
options: Leave cooked food uncovered near flies
Use the same unwashed board for raw meat and fruit
Taste food to test whether it is safe
questions.explanation: Handwashing reduces transfer of germs to food.

questions.question: Which nutrient is especially important for healthy bones and teeth?
questions.explanation: Calcium is a key mineral in bones and teeth.

questions.question: A lack of iron can lead to which condition?
questions.explanation: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; deficiency can cause anaemia.

questions.question: Why should we drink safe water regularly?
options: It removes the need for sleep
It supports body functions and prevents dehydration
It provides all nutrients in sufficient amounts
questions.explanation: Water is essential for transport, temperature regulation and other body processes.

questions.question: Which material is attracted to a magnet?
questions.explanation: Iron is a magnetic material.

questions.question: Which method separates insoluble sand from water?
questions.explanation: Filter paper traps sand while water passes through.

questions.question: How can salt be recovered from salt solution?
questions.explanation: Evaporation removes water and leaves salt behind.

questions.question: Which object is translucent?
questions.explanation: Translucent materials let some light through but do not form a clear image.

questions.question: Which material is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal and conducts electricity well.

questions.question: Which property makes aluminium useful for making cooking foil?
options: It is attracted strongly to magnets
It can be rolled into thin sheets
questions.explanation: Malleability allows aluminium to be made into thin sheets.

questions.question: A mixture contains iron filings and sand. Which is the simplest way to separate them?
questions.explanation: A magnet attracts the iron filings but not the sand.

questions.question: Which substance dissolves readily in water?
questions.explanation: Sugar dissolves in water to form a solution.

questions.question: Which is an example of an irreversible change?
questions.explanation: Burning creates new substances and cannot be reversed simply.

questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched with a separation method?
questions.explanation: A strainer or filter separates solid tea leaves from liquid tea.

questions.question: Which is the SI unit of length?
questions.explanation: The SI base unit for length is the metre.

questions.question: A cyclist travels 60 metres in 10 seconds. What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 m/s.

questions.question: Which motion repeats at regular intervals?
questions.explanation: Periodic motion repeats after equal time intervals.

questions.question: Which instrument measures time intervals in a race?
questions.explanation: A stopwatch measures elapsed time.

questions.question: A car moves along a straight road. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Rectilinear motion occurs along a straight line.

questions.question: The tip of a clock's second hand moves in what path?
questions.explanation: The hand rotates around the clock's centre, tracing a circle.

questions.question: If the same distance is covered in less time, average speed is
questions.explanation: Speed increases when distance stays fixed and time decreases.

questions.question: Which reading is most suitable for a room's temperature?
questions.explanation: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius in everyday settings.

questions.question: Why should the eye be level with the liquid surface when reading a measuring cylinder?
questions.explanation: Eye-level reading reduces parallax error.

questions.question: A runner completes one full lap of a circular track and returns to the start. What is the displacement?
questions.explanation: Displacement is zero when the final position equals the initial position.

questions.question: Light usually travels in which way through a uniform transparent medium?
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines in a uniform medium.

questions.question: Which object is luminous?
questions.explanation: A luminous object produces its own light.

questions.question: A shadow forms when light is blocked by an
questions.explanation: An opaque object blocks light and creates a shadow.

questions.question: Which surface gives the clearest regular reflection?
questions.explanation: A smooth surface reflects light in an orderly way.

questions.question: The Moon appears bright mainly because it
questions.explanation: The Moon reflects light from the Sun.

questions.question: Which is needed for a shadow to form?
options: Light source, opaque object and screen or surface
questions.explanation: A shadow appears where an opaque object blocks light from reaching a surface.

questions.question: Sound is produced by
questions.explanation: Vibrating objects produce sound.

questions.question: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?
options: It always travels only through water
Sound is a type of shadow
It needs a material medium to carry vibrations
questions.explanation: Sound requires particles to transmit vibrations.

questions.question: Which material is likely to absorb more sound and reduce echoes?
questions.explanation: Soft porous materials absorb more sound than hard smooth surfaces.

questions.question: Which action can make a guitar string produce a sound?
options: Pluck the string so it vibrates
questions.explanation: Plucking makes the string vibrate and produce sound.

questions.question: What is needed to make a simple electric circuit work?
options: A plastic loop with no cell
A closed conducting path with a cell and component
questions.explanation: Current flows in a complete circuit with a source of electrical energy.

questions.question: Which material is an electrical insulator?
questions.explanation: Rubber resists the flow of electric current.

questions.question: What happens when a switch opens a simple circuit?
questions.explanation: An open circuit interrupts the conducting path.

questions.question: Which poles of two magnets attract each other?
questions.explanation: North and south poles attract; like poles repel.

questions.question: Where is a bar magnet's magnetic effect strongest?
questions.explanation: Magnetic forces are strongest near the poles.

questions.question: Which item can act as a temporary magnet when wrapped with wire carrying current?
questions.explanation: An electric current in a coil can magnetise an iron nail temporarily.

questions.question: Which safety action is correct around electrical appliances?
options: Touch bare wires to test current
Keep hands dry when touching switches
questions.explanation: Dry hands and intact insulation reduce electric-shock risk.

questions.question: In a circuit diagram, why are symbols used?
options: To represent components clearly and consistently
To make wires carry more current
questions.explanation: Standard symbols make circuit diagrams easier to read.

questions.question: A bulb does not glow in a circuit. Which is a sensible first check?
options: Remove every wire and leave it disconnected
Assume the bulb is too bright
Check whether the circuit is closed and connections are secure
questions.explanation: Loose connections or an open switch can stop current.

questions.question: Which statement about a freely suspended bar magnet is correct?
options: It points towards the nearest light source
It tends to align roughly north–south
questions.explanation: Earth's magnetic field makes a freely suspended magnet align roughly north–south.

questions.question: Which action helps reduce plastic waste?
options: Reuse suitable items and recycle where facilities exist
Use a new disposable bag for every item
questions.explanation: Reducing and reusing materials prevents waste before recycling.

questions.question: Which gas do plants release during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is released when plants photosynthesise.

questions.question: Which is a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Sunlight is replenished naturally and is renewable.

questions.question: What is the main cause of day and night on Earth?
options: The Moon blocks the Sun every evening
The Sun circles Earth once each day
questions.explanation: Earth's rotation causes different places to face towards or away from the Sun.

questions.question: Which practice conserves water at home?
options: Leave the tap running while brushing
Wash one cup under a running tap for ten minutes
questions.explanation: Repairing leaks prevents unnecessary water loss.

questions.question: Which is a producer in a food chain?
questions.explanation: Green plants make their own food and are producers.

questions.question: What is the main role of decomposers in an ecosystem?
options: Break down dead organisms and recycle nutrients
questions.explanation: Decomposers return nutrients to the environment by breaking down dead matter.

questions.question: Which event is caused by the Moon's gravity acting on Earth's oceans, together with the Sun's influence?
questions.explanation: Gravitational forces from the Moon and Sun cause ocean tides.

questions.question: Why should e-waste not be mixed casually with household rubbish?
options: It can contain hazardous materials and needs suitable handling
It turns into clean water immediately
questions.explanation: Electronic waste can contain materials that require specialised collection and recycling.

questions.question: Which observation best supports that air occupies space?
options: An inverted empty-looking cup traps air and resists filling fully underwater
questions.explanation: Trapped air prevents water from immediately filling the cup.

questions.question: A student observes that a metal spoon feels colder than a wooden spoon in the same room. What best explains this?
options: Metal is always at a lower temperature
Metal conducts heat away from the hand faster
questions.explanation: Metal conducts heat more readily, so it draws heat from the hand faster.

questions.question: A shadow is shortest around noon on a sunny day because
options: The Sun is relatively high in the sky
The Sun turns off at noon
questions.explanation: A higher Sun angle produces a shorter shadow.

questions.question: Four seedlings receive equal water, soil and light, but one gets no light. Which comparison best tests light's effect?
options: Give each seedling different soil and water
Change the seed type every day
Measure only the colour of the pots
Compare the growth of the seedling kept without light with the others
questions.explanation: Keeping other factors similar makes the light comparison fair.

questions.question: A mixture contains rice grains, iron pins and salt. Which sequence is most suitable to separate all three?
options: Filter once and collect everything together
Use only a magnet to remove all three
Use a magnet for pins, sieve rice, then dissolve and evaporate salt solution
Freeze the mixture and shake it
questions.explanation: Magnetism separates iron, size can separate rice, and evaporation can recover dissolved salt.

questions.question: A toy car travels 12 m in 4 s and then 12 m in 2 s. During which part is it faster?
options: It is stationary in both parts
questions.explanation: The first speed is 3 m/s and the second is 6 m/s.

questions.question: A student sees a plant bend towards a window. This response is called
questions.explanation: Phototropism is plant growth in response to light direction.

questions.question: A torch beam is aimed at a wall. An opaque book is placed in the beam. What appears on the wall?
options: A dark shadow where light is blocked
questions.explanation: The book blocks light from reaching part of the wall.

questions.question: A compass needle changes direction near a bar magnet because
options: The magnet changes the air into water
The magnet exerts a magnetic force on the needle
The needle is attracted by sunlight
questions.explanation: A compass needle is magnetic and responds to nearby magnetic fields.

questions.question: A student wants to compare how quickly sugar dissolves in cold and warm water. Which is the fairest setup?
options: Use more sugar in the cold water
Use equal water volumes and sugar amounts, changing only water temperature
Use different cups with unknown volumes
questions.explanation: Changing only temperature allows a fair comparison of dissolving rate.

questions.question: Which conclusion is best after one seed fails to germinate?
options: One failure alone does not prove that the seed type can never germinate
All seeds of this type are dead
Water is never needed by seeds
The seed has become an animal
questions.explanation: A single result is not enough; check conditions and repeat with more seeds.
